name: R. Albert Mohler Jr.
bio: R. Albert Mohler Jr. is the ninth president of The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary and one of the leading intellectuals of the evangelical movement in America. A prolific author and podcaster, he addresses Christian worldview issues and theological controversies facing the contemporary church.
education: PhD in Systematic & Historical Theology, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary

name: Everett L. Worthington Jr.
bio:
Everett L. Worthington Jr., Ph.D., is a pioneering forgiveness researcher and Commonwealth Professor Emeritus at Virginia Commonwealth University, where he conducted over 35 years of scientific study on forgiveness before retiring in 2017. A clinical psychologist and committed Christian, Worthington developed the REACH Forgiveness method (with colleagues Michael McCullough and Steve Sandage), which has been tested in over 22 randomized clinical trials globally and is one of the two most-studied approaches to promoting forgiveness.

Worthing's personal faith deepened in 1996 when his mother was murdered, an experience that shaped his conviction that forgiveness and reconciliation must flow from Christian spirituality. His work integrates psychological rigor with theological depth, particularly in his revised book Forgiving and Reconciling: Bridges to Wholeness and Hope, which demonstrates how Christian theology undergirds the science of forgiveness, making him an essential voice for evangelicals seeking to understand reconciliation.

name: James Abernathy
bio: James Abernathy is a writer for The Gospel Coalition whose work engages disability theology, embodiment, and the full inclusion of people with disabilities in the life of the church. He writes with personal insight and theological care about what it means to bear the image of God in all its diversity.

name: Guardian staff and agencies
bio: A shared byline used by The Guardian for wire-service and staff reporting on international news stories. Represents collective journalism across the organization's newsroom.

name: Richard Luscombe and agency
bio: Richard Luscombe is a Christian content creator and agency leader dedicated to helping churches and ministries communicate their faith-based messages effectively. Through his agency work, he partners with Christian organizations to develop strategic content that resonates with evangelical audiences.

name: Randy Alcorn
bio:
Randy Alcorn is a prolific Christian author, speaker, and founder of Eternal Perspective Ministries (founded 1990), a nonprofit dedicated to teaching biblical truth and helping the needy. After serving as co-pastor of Good Shepherd Community Church in Oregon for fourteen years, Alcorn transitioned to focus on writing and speaking—his primary calling. With more than 60 books translated into over 70 languages and articles distributed in 34 languages beyond English, Alcorn has become one of evangelicalism's most widely-read authors.

His major works include Heaven and If God Is Good: Faith in the Midst of Suffering and Evil, which have sold widely and shaped evangelical thinking about eternal hope and theodicy. A popular conference speaker and part-time faculty member at Western Seminary and Multnomah University, Alcorn combines pastoral warmth with intellectual rigor, addressing both spiritual encouragement and deep theological questions for a broad evangelical readership.

name: Chris Allen
bio: Baptist minister with experience in church leadership roles including as Licensed Local Pastor and liaison to associational partnerships.
education: M.A. in Christian Ministry & Leadership, Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary

name: Matthew Lee Anderson
bio: Matthew Lee Anderson is an Associate Professor of Ethics and Theology in Baylor University's Honors College and founder of Mere Orthodoxy. He is the author of several books addressing Christian ethics and co-hosts the Mere Fidelity podcast on theology and culture.
education: DPhil in Christian Ethics, Oxford University

name: Tony Arsenal
bio: Tony Arsenal is a co-host of the Reformed Brotherhood Podcast and maintains the Reformed Arsenal blog exploring Reformed theology and biblical studies. He holds Master of Arts degrees in Church History and Theology.
education: Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary (MA Church History and Theology)

name: Sara Atske
bio: Sara Atske is a researcher and writer focused on faith, culture, and social trends. Her work explores how Christian perspectives intersect with contemporary issues and cultural conversations.

name: Michelle Ayres
bio: Unable to find definitive information on a prominent Christian writer by this exact name. Search results suggest possible confusion with Dr. Michelle Ami Reyes, an Indian American Christian writer whose work appears in Christianity Today, or with Michelle Ayres LMFT, a therapist and co-author of The Decider Skills.

name: John Baker
bio:
John Baker (1948-2021) was the founder of Celebrate Recovery, a revolutionary Christ-centered 12-step program that destigmatized addiction and recovery in evangelical churches. After struggling with his own alcoholism and finding that secular AA meetings offered no space for faith while church small groups offered no safe place for discussing addiction, Baker created a biblical alternative at Saddleback Church in 1991 that bridged both worlds.

Combining Christian principles with the proven 12-step structure, Celebrate Recovery grew to impact over 7 million people across 35,000 churches worldwide, fundamentally changing how evangelicals address recovery and brokenness. Baker's legacy redefined evangelical compassion and vulnerability, opening church doors to those struggling with addiction, codependency, and other life-controlling issues. He died unexpectedly in February 2021 at age 72, leaving behind a movement that continues to demonstrate Christ's healing power.

name: Nick Batzig
bio: Nick Batzig is a contributing editor at Ligonier Ministries and serves as pastor of New Covenant Presbyterian Church (PCA) in Richmond Hill, Georgia. A thoughtful expositor and Reformed theologian, he writes on covenant theology, biblical typology, and the doctrines of grace.

name: Voddie Baucham
bio:
Voddie Baucham is a Reformed theologian, pastor, author, and educator who served as founding dean of the School of Divinity at African Christian University in Lusaka, Zambia (2015-2024). His work emphasizes family discipleship and multi-generational faithfulness through family-integrated ministry, articulated in his influential book Family Driven Faith: Doing What It Takes to Raise Sons and Daughters Who Walk with God (2007).

Baucham's advocacy for family-integrated churches—where families worship and receive formation together rather than separated by age—has shaped evangelical approaches to family ministry and discipleship. He served as board member of the National Center for Family-Integrated Churches and moved his family to Zambia to demonstrate his commitment to gospel-centered family formation and global Christian education. His ministry demonstrates the integration of biblical theology, cultural engagement, and family as the primary vehicle for Christian discipleship.
education: Houston Baptist University (BA); Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary (MDiv); Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary (DMin)

name: Taylor Berry
bio: Taylor Berry is a freelance journalist and content professional with over five years of experience in storytelling and narrative journalism. Her byline has appeared in Paste Magazine, Distractify, and other publications covering entertainment, pop culture, and arts topics.
affiliation: Freelance; contributed to Paste Magazine, Distractify, Rising Artists Music Agency

name: Matthew Mpoke Bigg
bio: Matthew Mpoke Bigg is a theologian and biblical scholar who brings deep insight into Scripture and Christian doctrine. His work emphasizes the richness of biblical theology and its application to contemporary Christian life and witness.

name: Ginger Blomberg
bio: Ginger Blomberg is a writer for The Gospel Coalition who covers international Christianity, church growth, and mission. Her reporting brings attention to the global body of Christ, particularly stories of faith flourishing in places where the gospel is spreading rapidly.

name: Todd Boone
bio: Todd Boone is a pastor and writer contributing to Reformation21, the online journal of the Alliance of Confessing Evangelicals. He writes on biblical exposition, Reformed theology, and the spiritual significance of the church calendar and ordinances.

name: Paige Brady
bio: Paige Brady is a pastor specializing in ministry to older adults and end-of-life care. Her evangelical perspective integrates traditional Christian practices (prayer, Scripture, confession) with modern palliative care approaches. Brady helps congregations develop thoughtful, biblically-grounded practices around death preparation and dying well.

name: Elise Brandon
bio: Copy editor and writer with experience in Christian publishing, editing Bible studies and content for Christian organizations.

name: Chris Brauns
bio: Chris Brauns is a pastor, author, and advocate for church leadership and biblical community. He has written extensively on topics including church discipline, conflict resolution, and spiritual formation, bringing both theological insight and practical wisdom to his work.

books.title: Unpacking Forgiveness: Biblical Answers to Life's Toughest Questions
Stragglers: Why Young Adults Leave the Church and Rethink Faith
The Pastor's Practical Guide to Church Discipline

name: Reuben Bredenhof
bio: Reuben Bredenhof is a pastor and Christian writer committed to helping believers understand Scripture and live out their faith in the modern world. His writing emphasizes practical theology and biblical worldview formation for contemporary Christians.

name: Thomas Brewer
bio: Thomas Brewer is resident adjunct professor at Reformation Bible College and vice president of publishing at Ligonier Ministries. He is a teaching elder in the Presbyterian Church in America.

name: Cory Brock
bio: Cory Brock is a pastor, author, and speaker who seeks to help Christians think deeply about their faith and culture. He serves as senior pastor at Antioch Community Church in Nashville, Tennessee, and is known for thoughtful biblical teaching that engages contemporary questions.
affiliation: Antioch Community Church (Nashville); Various Christian publications
education: PhD in Systematic Theology, University of St. Andrews

books.title: Theססential Church: Reclaiming a Christianity the World Never Forgot
Heavenly Minded: The Pursuit of a Christian Worldview
God is a Drinker: Finding Delight in the Divine Goodness

name: Bethany Broderick
bio: Writer, speaker, and assistant professor of marketing who addresses Christian living and faith. Author of Perfected: Trading Shame and Striving for Wholeness in Christ.

books.title: Perfected: Trading Shame and Striving for Wholeness in Christ

name: Emily Brown
bio: Emily M. Brown is an ordained pastor and preacher who earned her Master of Divinity from Union Theological Seminary in 2010, receiving the David H. C. Read Memorial Preacher/Scholar Award for excellence in preaching and biblical scholarship. She has served as Pastoral Associate at Broadway United Church of Christ and as Community Minister at Judson Memorial Church in New York City.
affiliation: Broadway United Church of Christ, Judson Memorial Church
education: Master of Divinity, Union Theological Seminary (2010)

name: Michael L. Brown
bio:
Michael L. Brown is an American apologist, radio host, author, and proponent of Messianic Judaism and the Charismatic movement. Holding a Ph.D. in Near Eastern Languages and Literatures from New York University, Brown has served as visiting or adjunct professor at numerous institutions including Southern Evangelical Seminary, Gordon-Conwell, Trinity Evangelical Divinity School, and Fuller Seminary. His nationally syndicated radio show The Line of Fire reaches audiences throughout the United States addressing apologetics, cultural issues, and biblical faith.

Widely recognized as the world's foremost Messianic Jewish apologist, Brown has debated Jewish rabbis, secular professors, and activists on radio, television, and college campuses. In the mid-1990s, he became a leader in the Brownsville Revival charismatic outpouring in Florida. His prolific writing and speaking engage contemporary culture with biblical wisdom while addressing controversy and defending Christian truth claims.
education: Cedarville University (BA); Trinity Evangelical Divinity School (MDiv)

name: John Bryce
bio: John T. Brice, M.Div., is Lead Pastor at the Historic Tindley Temple and a committed visionary focused on community, family, and youth development. An alumnus of Morehouse College and member of Philadelphia's Commission on African-American Males, he serves multiple community leadership organizations.

name: Ryan Burge
bio: Ryan Burge is a political scientist and statistician at Washington University in St. Louis specializing in the study of religion's impact on American politics and society. His research on religious demographics and the rise of the religiously unaffiliated has shaped how evangelicals understand cultural change.
education: PhD in Political Science, Southern Illinois University

books.title: 20 Myths about Religion and Politics in America

name: Josh Burnett
bio: Josh Burnett is a writer and ministry practitioner contributing to the Carey Nieuwhof platform, where he addresses church leadership, preaching, and ministry strategy. His work helps pastors think through the practical and theological dimensions of sermon preparation and congregational discipleship.

name: Aimee Byrd
bio: Aimee Byrd is an author, speaker, and Bible study teacher who writes about theology, biblical womanhood, and evangelical culture. She is known for her theological depth and challenges to shallow women's ministry resources, and regularly contributes to Christianity Today.

books.title: Recovering from Biblical Manhood and Womanhood

name: Katy Carl
bio: Katy Carl is an author and editor known for contemporary Catholic literary fiction. She is editor-in-chief of Dappled Things literary magazine, editor of Luminor at Word on Fire, and writer in residence at the University of St. Thomas in Houston, with extensive experience in Catholic publishing.
affiliation: Dappled Things, Word on Fire, University of St. Thomas Houston, Saint Mary's Press
role: Author, editor, and writer in residence

books.title: Praying the Great O Antiphons: My Soul Magnifies the Lord

name: Jamie Carlson
bio: Jamie Carlson is a writer at Mere Orthodoxy who engages questions of gender, theology, and evangelical culture with careful attention to both Scripture and tradition. Her essays call for more substantive theological engagement in evangelical debates that are often reduced to political or cultural terms.

name: Charles Carman
bio: Assistant Professor of History at Regent University specializing in Byzantine theology, Syriac studies, and ancient church history with published work in The American Conservative.
education: Doctoral student in Syriac and Church History, Catholic University of America

name: Roberto Carrera
bio: Roberto Carrera is a Christian author and speaker dedicated to sharing biblical wisdom with Spanish-speaking and Latino communities. His work emphasizes faith, discipleship, and practical Christian living for modern believers.

name: Kara Bettis Carvalho
bio: Senior features editor at Christianity Today covering religion and culture. Award-winning religion journalist known for reported profiles and narrative features.
education: Bachelor of Arts in Media Studies from The King's College; Master of Arts in Theology from Southern Baptist Theological Seminary

name: Francis Chan
bio:
Francis Chan is an American pastor, author, and speaker who founded the nondenominational Cornerstone Community Church in Simi Valley, California (1994) and served as its teaching pastor for sixteen years before stepping away from the megachurch model in 2010. His New York Times bestselling book Crazy Love: Overwhelmed by a Relentless God (2008) challenged evangelicals to move beyond "lukewarm Christianity" and sparked a generational conversation about radical discipleship and countercultural faith, selling millions of copies globally.

Beyond Cornerstone, Chan founded Eternity Bible College (2004) and has authored multiple books including Letters to the Church and Until Unity. Though he stepped back from the megachurch spotlight in recent years, his prophetic voice calling believers to deeper commitment to Jesus continues to influence evangelical thought and practice, particularly among younger Christians seeking authentic spiritual transformation.
education: Valley Christian Schools (credential); Biola University (honorary Doctor)

name: Cassandra Vinograd and Oleksandr Chubko
bio: Journalists at The New York Times who co-report from Eastern Europe, covering conflict and geopolitical stories including the war in Ukraine and its impact on civilians.

name: R. Scott Clark
bio:
R. Scott Clark is a Reformed theologian, pastor, and Professor of Church History and Historical Theology at Westminster Seminary California, where he has taught since 1997. After serving as academic dean (1997-2001), Clark distinguished himself as a careful historian of Reformed doctrine and practice. Holding degrees from the University of Nebraska (BA), Westminster Seminary California (MDiv), and St. Anne's College, Oxford University (DPhil), he brings both pastoral and scholarly expertise.

Clark is series co-editor for Classic Reformed Theology (Reformation Heritage Books) and founder of the Heidelberg Reformation Association, the Heidelcast podcast, and the widely-read Heidelblog. His publications include The Heidelberg Catechism: A Historical, Theological, and Pastoral Commentary, Recovering the Reformed Confession, and studies on covenant theology and Reformed orthodoxy, making him a significant voice in contemporary Reformed evangelical theology and church history.
education: Wheaton College (BA); Fordham University (MA); University of Wales (PhD)

name: Joy Marie Clarkson
bio: Joy Marie Clarkson is a writer, podcaster, and researcher at King's College London specializing in theology and literature. Books and Culture Editor at Plough Quarterly, she explores art, theology, and contemporary culture through her published works and popular podcast.

name: Timon Cline
bio: Timon Cline is editor-in-chief of American Reformer and an attorney specializing in law and theology. He is a fellow at the Craig Center at Westminster Theological Seminary and director of Scholarly Initiatives at the Hale Institute.
affiliation: American Reformer; Westminster Theological Seminary; Hale Institute
education: Wright State University (BA); Rutgers Law School (JD); Westminster Theological Seminary (Graduate)

name: Darrell Cole
bio:
Darrell Cole is Associate Professor of Religion and Chair of the Department of Comparative Religion at Drew University, specializing in Christian ethics with particular focus on just war theory and the ethics of warfare. Holding master's degrees in philosophy (Ohio University) and religion (Yale University), plus a doctorate in theology (Duke University) and PhD from the University of Virginia, Cole brings rigorous academic training to the intersection of ethics and theology.

Cole's scholarly work examines the progressive development of just war theory from biblical foundations through medieval Catholic and Reformation theological traditions. His books, including Just War and the Ethics of Espionage and When God Says War Is Right, provide evangelical and broader Christian audiences with sophisticated theological frameworks for thinking about the ethics of military conflict, making him an important voice in evangelical political theology.
education: Wheaton College (BA); Trinity Evangelical Divinity School (MDiv); University of Virginia (PhD)

books.title: The God of Peace and the God of War

name: John Mark Comer
bio:
John Mark Comer is a pastor, teacher, New York Times bestselling author, and founder of Practicing the Way, a nonprofit ministry dedicated to forming lifelong apprentices of Jesus. After serving as founding pastor of Bridgetown Church in Portland, Oregon for nearly two decades—during which he pioneered a church-wide emphasis on spiritual formation—Comer stepped away in 2021 to expand his teaching through Practicing the Way, which creates free formation resources for churches worldwide.

His books, including the bestselling Practicing the Way and The Ruthless Elimination of Hurry, articulate a vision of spiritual life centered on three goals: be with Jesus, become like Jesus, and do what he did. Through his teaching, writing, and ministry platform, Comer has become one of evangelicalism's most important voices calling believers back to contemplative spirituality and intentional discipleship, particularly resonating with younger Christians seeking depth over busyness.

name: William Conley
bio: William Henry Conley (1840-1897) was a Pittsburgh philanthropist and industrialist who provided organizational and financial support to religious institutions. He was the first president of Zion's Watch Tower Tract Society, a member of the Christian and Missionary Alliance board, and instrumental in funding religious missions and organizations internationally.
affiliation: Christian and Missionary Alliance, Zion's Watch Tower Tract Society

name: Brandon Corley
bio: Biblical studies graduate and MDiv student at Southern Baptist Theological Seminary. Contributor to American Reformer on Christian theology and reform.
education: The Master's University (BA Biblical Studies); Southern Baptist Theological Seminary (MDiv student)

name: Brittany Dahl
bio: Educator with master's degree in Elementary Education and 10+ years classroom experience. Created The Miraculous Journey of Books to help families build lasting relationships through reading.
education: Master's in Elementary Education with Reading Endorsement

name: Mark Dever
bio:
Mark E. Dever (born August 28, 1960) is a theologian and the senior pastor of Capitol Hill Baptist Church in Washington, D.C. since 1994, and president emeritus of 9Marks, the influential ministry he founded in 1998. Holding an M.Div. from Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary, a Th.M. from Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, and a Ph.D. in Ecclesiastical History from Cambridge University, Dever brings scholarly depth to pastoral ministry.

Through 9Marks, Dever has reshaped evangelical church practice by articulating nine marks of a healthy church: expositional preaching, biblical theology, gospel-centered understanding, regenerate membership, biblical church discipline, biblical evangelism, biblical leadership, biblical church membership, and passionate prayer. His work has profoundly influenced how evangelicals understand church health, polity, and leadership, making him one of the most significant voices in contemporary evangelical ecclesiology.
education: University of North Carolina (BA); Southern Seminary (MDiv); Cambridge University (PhD)

name: Kevin DeYoung
bio:
Kevin DeYoung is Associate Professor of Systematic Theology at Reformed Theological Seminary Charlotte and senior pastor of Christ Covenant Church in Matthews, North Carolina. After earning his Ph.D. in early modern history from the University of Leicester (UK), DeYoung joined RTS in 2017 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2021. His works have won multiple Christianity Today Book Awards, including Why We're Not Emergent (2009), Why We Love the Church (2010), and Crazy Busy (2014).

Through his pastoral leadership, academic teaching, and prolific writing, DeYoung has shaped contemporary evangelical theology, particularly regarding church practices, biblical sexuality, and Reformed doctrine. Elected moderator of the PCA's 52nd General Assembly in 2025, he represents a new generation of evangelical leaders committed to doctrinal faithfulness, pastoral care, and cultural engagement grounded in Scripture and Reformed theology.

name: Julie Dickerson
bio: Julie Dickerson is pursuing a Master of Biblical and Theological Studies from Dallas Theological Seminary, currently serving as a Bible study leader, teacher, and writer. Based in College Station, Texas, she mentors and disciples young women through her teaching and theological work.
role: Bible study leader, teacher, and theological writer
education: M.A. in Biblical and Theological Studies (in progress), Dallas Theological Seminary

name: Courtney Doctor
bio: Director of Women's Initiatives at The Gospel Coalition and author of Bible studies and theological works exploring Scripture and Christian discipleship.

books.title: Titus: Displaying the Gospel of Grace

name: Jonathan K. Dodson
bio:
Jonathan K. Dodson (MDiv, ThM) is the founding pastor of City Life Church in Austin, Texas, and founder of Gospel-Centered Discipleship, an online platform producing resources to help churches make, mature, and multiply disciples of Jesus. Partnering with his wife Robie, Dodson also co-founded The Fair Deed Project, demonstrating his commitment to integration of gospel proclamation and justice work.

Dodson's signature book Gospel-Centered Discipleship (now in its second revised and expanded edition) provides a practical, reproducible model for small gospel-centered discipleship groups that combine theological depth with missional focus. His work emphasizes how the gospel redefines discipleship while addressing sin, maintaining Christ-centrality, and creating sustainable kingdom community, making him an important voice for a generation of evangelicals seeking to revitalize discipleship beyond traditional models.

name: Marina Dunbar
bio: Marina Dunbar is a journalist and Guardian US Fellow at The Guardian, with expertise in health, science, and investigative reporting developed during her master's at Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism. Based in New York, she brings reporting experience from local California outlets and health journalism.
education: Master of Journalism, Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism at CUNY (2022-2023)

name: Ligon Duncan
bio: Ligon Duncan is a Reformed theologian, pastor, and author deeply committed to expository preaching and biblical scholarship. He has served as senior pastor of Christ Church in Jackson, Mississippi, and is known for his work in promoting confessional Reformed theology and historical Christian thought. Through teaching, writing, and pastoral ministry, Duncan seeks to help believers understand and apply Scripture with doctrinal depth and practical wisdom.
affiliation: Christ Church Jackson; Reformed Theological Seminary
education: M.A.R., Westminster Theological Seminary; Ph.D., University of Edinburgh

books.title: Does the Bible Really Say That?

name: Kent Dunnington
bio:
Kent Dunnington is an Associate Professor of Philosophy at Biola University where he teaches ethics, logic, and the philosophy of addiction. Holding a PhD from Texas A&M and an MTS in theology from Duke University, Dunnington brings rigorous philosophical training to questions of human virtue and vice, particularly addiction and moral psychology.

His first book Addiction and Virtue: Beyond the Models of Disease and Choice (2011) offers an interdisciplinary philosophical-theological analysis drawing on Aristotle and Thomas Aquinas to develop an alternative to reductionistic models of addiction. His second work Humility, Pride, and Christian Virtue Theory (Oxford UP, 2019) continues his exploration of virtue ethics and theological anthropology. Dunnington's work is particularly informed by his experiences teaching in prisons, bringing lived perspective to abstract philosophical questions about human freedom, vice, and redemption.

books.title: Humility, Pride, and Christian Virtue Theory

name: Sidney Dyer
bio: Sidney Dyer is a writer and editor contributing to Ligonier Ministries, where he explores Reformed theology, the doctrine of God, and topics in systematic and biblical theology. His work serves readers seeking rigorous engagement with the classic doctrines of the Christian faith.

name: Aaron Earls
bio: Senior writer at LifeWay Christian Resources covering church trends, pastoral issues, and American Christianity. His work appears in Baptist Press, The Gospel Coalition, ChurchLeaders, and other Christian media.

name: Doug Eaton
bio: Associate Vice President of Enrollment at Trinity International University and adjunct faculty member specializing in theology and Christian apologetics.

name: Arla Eicher
bio: Wife of Nick Eicher, Arla is part of a household known for biblical journalism and Christian media work. The couple lives in St. Louis with five children and two granddaughters, and Arla supports evangelical journalism through her partnership with her husband's work at WORLD magazine.
role: Christian household partner and supporter of evangelical journalism

name: Annie Eisner
bio: Christian writer at RELEVANT Magazine exploring contemporary Christian culture and theology. Addresses topics including manifesting in Christian culture and church hurt.

name: Rebecca F. Elliott
bio: Rebecca F. Elliott is a Christian author and illustrator known for creating children's books that celebrate faith, diversity, and God's love. Her work combines engaging storytelling with vibrant illustrations to help young readers explore biblical themes and Christian values in meaningful ways.

name: Douglas Farrow
bio:
Douglas Farrow is Professor of Theology and Ethics at McGill University in Montreal, where he has taught since 1998 and serves as holder of the Kennedy Smith Chair in Catholic Studies. After completing his doctorate under Colin Gunton at King's College London and teaching there, Farrow brings a distinctly Catholic theological perspective to discussions of ecclesiology, political theology, and soteriology that evangelical readers increasingly find valuable.

Farrow's scholarly work draws inspiration from patristic and medieval sources—Augustine, Anselm, Aquinas, and John Paul II—while engaging contemporary church and state issues. His major works include Ascension Theology (T&T Clark 2011) and Desiring a Better Country: Forays in Political Theology (McGill-Queens 2015). He is a regular interlocutor with evangelical and ecumenical groups through organizations like the Institute on Religion and Public Life and Evangelicals and Catholics Together, making him a bridge-builder between Catholic and evangelical thought.
education: Harvard University (BA); McMaster Divinity College (MPhil, PhD)

name: Nate Fischer
bio: Nate Fischer is Chairman of American Reformer and founder and CEO of New Founding, a venture firm focused on Christian-centered American revitalization. A Harvard Law graduate, he writes on evangelical leadership and Christian cultural engagement.
education: JD, Harvard Law School; BA, Calvin College

name: Gabriel N.E. Fluhrer
bio: Senior Pastor of First Presbyterian Church in Chattanooga and adjunct professor of systematic theology, writing on biblical themes and Christian faith.
affiliation: First Presbyterian Church, Chattanooga; Reformed Theological Seminary
role: Senior Pastor; Adjunct Professor of Systematic Theology
education: M.Div., Greenville Presbyterian Theological Seminary; Ph.D., Westminster Theological Seminary

books.title: Alive: How the Resurrection of Christ Changes Everything

name: Danny Franks
bio: Danny Franks is the Pastor of Guest Services at The Summit Church in Durham, North Carolina, overseeing hospitality across ten campuses. He is an author and consultant helping churches welcome guests with gospel-centered hospitality.

name: Angela Fulton
bio: Southeast Asia editor for Christianity Today and former managing editor at World Magazine. Writes on religion and Christian perspectives across major Christian publications.

books.title: I Choose To Pray For My Husband

name: Stan Gale
bio: Stan Gale is a pastor and Christian author dedicated to helping believers grow in their faith and understanding of Scripture. His writing and ministry focus on practical discipleship and spiritual formation for modern Christians.

name: Christopher Gehrz
bio: Christopher Gehrz is professor of history at Bethel University in St. Paul, Minnesota, and the author of The Pietist Vision of Christian Higher Education. He blogs at The Pietist Schoolman and writes on church history, the Pietist tradition, and the relationship between faith and scholarship. His work at Mere Orthodoxy brings a historian's perspective to evangelical self-understanding.

books.title: The Pietist Vision of Christian Higher Education

name: Peter J. Gentry
bio: Peter J. Gentry is a biblical scholar and theologian known for his work in Old Testament studies and biblical interpretation. He has contributed significantly to evangelical understanding of Scripture through his academic research and teaching.
education: Ph.D. in Old Testament, University of Stellenbosch

name: Benjamin L. Gladd
bio: Executive director of The Carson Center for Theological Renewal at The Gospel Coalition and former professor of New Testament at Reformed Theological Seminary. PhD from Wheaton College.

books.title: From Adam and Israel to the Church

name: Thomas Goodwin
bio: Thomas Goodwin (1600-1680) was an English Puritan theologian, preacher, and important leader of religious Independents. He served as chaplain to Oliver Cromwell and President of Magdalen College, Oxford.
education: Christ's College, Cambridge; Catharine Hall, Cambridge

books.title: The Heart of Christ in Heaven towards Sinners on Earth

name: Michael J. Gorman
bio:
Michael J. Gorman (born 1955) is the Raymond E. Brown Professor of Biblical Studies and Theology at St. Mary's Seminary and University in Baltimore, where he has taught since 1991. A New Testament scholar specializing in Pauline theology, Gorman is known for advancing the "participationist perspective" on Paul's theology—understanding salvation as participation in Christ—and brings ecumenical depth to evangelical biblical scholarship.

With a BA summa cum laude from Gordon College and a PhD from Princeton Theological Seminary, Gorman has authored twenty books and numerous articles on Paul, Revelation, the Gospel of John, and theological interpretation of Scripture. His election to the international Society for New Testament Studies, his role as editor of The Journal of Theological Interpretation, and his 2020 Festschrift recognition affirm his stature as a leading voice in contemporary biblical theology bridging evangelical and academic communities.
education: Wheaton College (BA); Duke University (MA); Durham University (PhD)

name: Joel B. Green
bio:
Joel B. Green (born May 7, 1956) is a leading New Testament scholar, theologian, and Associate Dean of the Center for Advanced Theological Study at Fuller Theological Seminary in Pasadena, California, where he serves as Professor of New Testament Interpretation. Holding a doctorate from the University of Aberdeen (1985), Green has distinguished himself through extensive research on Luke-Acts, the Gospels, 1 Peter, and James, as well as theological hermeneutics.

Credited with reshaping evangelical approaches to New Testament interpretation toward greater theological and missional depth, Green served as dean of Asbury Seminary and provost before joining Fuller. He is the general editor of the prestigious New International Commentary on the New Testament (NICNT) series, has authored or edited over 55 books (8 award-winning), and maintains membership in international scholarly societies including the Society for New Testament Studies and the International Society for Science and Religion, establishing him as a premier evangelical biblical scholar.
education: University of New England (BA); University of Aberdeen (PhD)

name: Adam Griffin
bio: Lead pastor at Eastside Community Church in Dallas with 20+ years in vocational ministry. Coauthor of Family Discipleship and host of The Family Discipleship Podcast.

name: Christina Grube
bio: Breaking News Reporter for WORLD News Group, a Christian media organization focused on reporting faith-related stories and issues.

name: Wayne Grudem
bio:
Wayne Grudem is Professor of Theology and Biblical Studies at Phoenix Seminary in Arizona, where he has taught since 2001 after more than twenty years at Trinity Evangelical Divinity School, where he chaired the Department of Biblical and Systematic Theology. A graduate of Harvard (BA), Westminster Seminary-Philadelphia (MDiv, DD), and the University of Cambridge (PhD), Grudem brings both evangelical passion and academic rigor to systematic theology.

His Systematic Theology: An Introduction to Biblical Doctrine, with over 750,000 copies sold and recently released in a revised and expanded second edition, stands as the most widely used systematic theology resource in evangelicalism. President of the Evangelical Theological Society (1999) and General Editor of the ESV Study Bible (ECPA Book of the Year 2009), Grudem has shaped evangelical theology and biblical interpretation. His integrative approach—combining careful exegesis, doctrinal precision, and practical application—has established him as one of evangelicalism's most authoritative theological voices.
education: Harvard (BA); Cambridge (MPhil); Trinity Evangelical Divinity School (DMin)

name: Nancy Guthrie
bio:
Nancy Guthrie is a Bible teacher, author, and podcast host from Franklin, Tennessee, who has devoted her ministry to helping Christians engage Scripture with both intellectual rigor and spiritual devotion. As host of the Help Me Teach the Bible podcast since 2015, Guthrie interviews excellent Bible teachers about how to teach specific biblical books and improve their approach to handling God's Word, making her a curator of evangelical biblical pedagogy.

Beyond the podcast, Guthrie teaches at Cornerstone Presbyterian Church and at conferences nationwide, including her signature Biblical Theology Workshop for Women. Her books and resources model careful biblical exposition combined with pastoral sensitivity, making her an influential voice among evangelical women especially, but valued across denominational and gender lines for her commitment to sound biblical teaching and effective communication.

name: Haleluya Hadero
bio: Haleluya Hadero is the Black Church Editor at Christianity Today, with a background in business and philanthropy reporting. Previously at The Associated Press, she investigated retail, technology, fossil fuel divestment, and racial equity giving, holding a degree from Columbia University's Graduate School of Journalism.
education: Graduate degree, Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism

name: Ashley Hales
bio: PhD in English from University of Edinburgh and Editorial Director for Print at Christianity Today. Author of Finding Holy in the Suburbs and A Spacious Life; Kirby Laing Centre Fellow.

name: M. Elizabeth Lewis Hall
bio: M. Elizabeth Lewis Hall is a professor of psychology at Rosemead School of Psychology at Biola University, where she researches the integration of Christian theology and psychological science. Her scholarly and popular writing addresses human embodiment, suffering, and what it means to be made in the image of God.
affiliation: Biola University / Rosemead School of Psychology

name: Gillis Harp
bio: Gillis Harp is a historian and author who specializes in American religious and intellectual history, with particular expertise in the development of Christian thought and culture. His scholarly work examines how faith has shaped American society and institutions throughout the nation's history. Harp combines rigorous historical research with accessible writing to help contemporary Christians understand their spiritual and cultural heritage.

books.title: Positivism and the Separation of Church and State: The Church in Nineteenth-Century America
Brahmin Prophet: Phillips Brooks and the Path of Liberal Protestantism

name: Ellen Hayes
bio: Ellen Hayes is a Christian author and speaker known for her work in faith-based content creation. She writes with a focus on spiritual encouragement and biblical living for contemporary Christian audiences.

name: Edward Helmore
bio: A journalist covering politics, government, and legal matters at The Guardian since 2010, with longstanding experience reporting on evolving news stories.

name: Chad Higgins
bio: A 15-year youth ministry veteran and co-founder of Youth Ministry Booster, dedicated to equipping churches and preventing burnout among youth workers.
role: Senior Manager of Church Equipping at Lifeway

name: Shelby Holliday
bio: Shelby Holliday is a journalist and on-air correspondent known for her work covering international news and faith-related stories with depth and integrity. Her reporting has taken her across the globe to document stories of resilience, hope, and human dignity from a perspective informed by Christian values.

name: Jason Horowitz
bio: Jason Horowitz is the Rome Bureau Chief of The New York Times, covering Italy, the Vatican, and southern Europe with emphasis on profiles and features. Previously a political correspondent at the Times and reporter at The Washington Post and New York Observer, his work has appeared in The New York Times Magazine, GQ, and Vogue.

name: John W. Hoyum
bio: John W. Hoyum is a pastor and writer at American Reformer who addresses the economic and institutional challenges facing the pastoral ministry. He advocates for fair compensation of clergy and writes on the health of the local church as an institution within broader society.

name: Scott Hubbard
bio: Scott Hubbard is a managing editor at Desiring God and pastor at All Peoples Church in Minneapolis. The author of over two hundred articles, he writes to deepen joy in God through Jesus, particularly for those navigating doubt and spiritual darkness.

name: Ben Hubbard
bio: Istanbul Bureau Chief at The New York Times and Middle East correspondent with over a decade of experience. Finalist for 2013 Pulitzer Prize in International Reporting for Syria coverage.
education: University of California, Berkeley (MA); Northwestern University (BA); American University in Cairo (Arabic Language & Literature)

name: Reuben Hunter
bio: Reuben Hunter is the lead pastor of Trinity West Church in London and a theological writer known for warm pastoral concern and cultural acumen. He contributes to The Gospel Coalition's Themelios journal and is involved with Acts 29, a church planting network, bringing thoughtful, profound perspective to Christian ministry.
affiliation: Trinity West Church London, The Gospel Coalition, Acts 29

books.title: God's Spirit: The Antidote to Chaos

name: Scott Hurst
bio: Pastor at Northminster Baptist Church in Toronto; maintains writing platform Write to Understand focusing on Christian theology and Canadian church history. Contributes to The Gospel Coalition, Servants of Grace, and For the Church.
education: Diploma from Antioch School of Church Planting and Leadership Development

name: Scott James
bio: Scott James is a pediatric infectious disease physician at University of Alabama at Birmingham and an author of children's books exploring Christian faith and illness. He serves as an elder at The Church at Brook Hills in Birmingham, Alabama.
role: Pediatric infectious disease physician and author
education: University of South Florida Morsani College of Medicine

books.title: The Expected One: Anticipating All of Jesus in the Advent
Mission Accomplished: A Two-Week Family Easter Devotional
God Cares for Me: Helping Children Trust God When They're Sick

name: Michael Jensen
bio: Michael Jensen is an Australian Anglican theologian and communicator known for making biblical scholarship accessible to everyday Christians. He has served as a minister and lecturer, contributing thoughtfully to contemporary Christian conversations about theology, faith, and cultural engagement.
affiliation: Anglican Church in Australia; Moore Theological College

books.title: Gravity and Grace: Understanding the Divine Nature
For the Love of God: A Journey Through the Bible

name: Emily Jensen
bio: Emily A. Jensen is an author, podcaster, and co-founder of Risen Motherhood, creating content that applies biblical truth to everyday life. Her first book, co-authored with her sister-in-law Laura, has sold over 100,000 copies and been translated into multiple languages, addressing Christian faith and motherhood.
affiliation: Risen Motherhood, The Gospel Coalition, Crossway Publishers

books.title: Risen Motherhood: Gospel Hope for Everyday Moments
He Is Strong: Devotions for When You Feel Weak

name: Reggie Joiner
bio:
Reggie Joiner is the founder and former CEO of Orange (reThink Group, Inc.), a nonprofit organization dedicated to helping churches maximize their influence on the next generation's spiritual growth. After eleven years as executive director of family ministry at Andy Stanley's North Point Community Church in Georgia, Joiner developed innovative family ministry models including KidStuf (bringing parents and children together to learn about God) and the Grow Up conference.

Through Orange, Joiner articulated the "Think Orange" philosophy—combining the strongest elements of church and family to create a revolutionary strategy affecting children's spiritual formation. His book Think Orange: Imagine the Impact When Church and Family Collide has shaped evangelical family ministry approaches. However, in April 2024, Joiner resigned following allegations of long-term sexual misconduct, significantly impacting his legacy and raising important conversations about accountability in evangelical leadership.

name: Timothy Paul Jones
bio: Timothy Paul Jones is the C. Edwin Gheens Professor of Christian Family Ministry and Vice President for Doctoral Studies at The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary. An evangelical scholar of apologetics and family ministry, he has authored or co-authored over twenty books making complex theological topics accessible to general audiences.

name: Mark Jones
bio: Mark Jones is a Reformed theologian and pastor known for making classical Christian doctrine accessible to contemporary audiences. His work emphasizes the practical application of theology to the Christian life, drawing from both Scripture and the rich heritage of Reformed thought.
affiliation: 謏Coral Ridge Presbyterian Church; Knowing Faith podcast

name: Kelly M. Kapic
bio: Kelly M. Kapic is professor of theological studies at Covenant College and a widely read voice in evangelical theology. He is the author of You're Only Human: How Your Limits Reflect God's Design and Why That's Good, Embodied Hope: A Theological Meditation on Pain and Suffering, and numerous other works. His scholarship bridges systematic theology and spiritual formation, helping Christians embrace their creaturely limitations as gifts from God.
education: PhD in Theology, King's College London

name: Stephen Kaufmann
bio: Stephen Kaufmann is a thoughtful Christian writer and speaker who explores faith, theology, and spiritual growth for contemporary audiences. His work encourages believers to deepen their understanding of Scripture and apply biblical principles to everyday life.

name: Tim Keller
affiliation: Redeemer Presbyterian Church; The Gospel Coalition
bio:
Timothy Keller (May 23, 1950 – May 19, 2023) was the founding pastor of Redeemer Presbyterian Church in Manhattan and co-founder of The Gospel Coalition, becoming one of evangelicalism's most influential voices in the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries. A pastor, apologist, theologian, and author, Keller modeled "winsome witness"—engaging contemporary culture with intellectual rigor and pastoral compassion while maintaining biblical conviction.

His New York Times bestselling books—The Prodigal God (2008) and The Reason for God (2008)—shaped evangelical thinking about grace, apologetics, and faith in a skeptical age. Through Redeemer's ministry, Redeemer City to City (training pastors globally), and his prolific writing, Keller demonstrated how Reformed theology addresses contemporary urban life and cultural challenges. His death on May 19, 2023, at age 72 from pancreatic cancer marked the end of a remarkable ministry that continues to influence evangelicals worldwide.
education: Bucknell University (BA); Gordon-Conwell (MDiv); Westminster Theological Seminary (DMin)

books.title: Forgive: Why Should I and How Can I?

name: R. T. Kendall
bio:
R. T. Kendall is an American evangelical theologian and minister born July 13, 1935, who served as Minister of Westminster Chapel in London from February 1, 1977, to February 1, 2002—a 25-year tenure that left a lasting imprint on the historic pulpit. After earning his BA from Trevecca Nazarene University, M.Div. from Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, and Ph.D. from the University of Oxford, Kendall brought both evangelical conviction and scholarly training to Westminster Chapel's pulpit.

During his ministry, Kendall led Westminster Chapel to embrace emphases and practices of the Charismatic renewal, demonstrating his openness to the Holy Spirit's contemporary gifting. His 1983 publication Once Saved, Always Saved sparked important theological debate about Christian perseverance. Retiring in 2002, Kendall authored over 50 books, including the influential Total Forgiveness, and through his speaking and ministry has been regarded as a statesman of the UK evangelical church.
education: Trevecca Nazarene; Southern Baptist Theological Seminary (MDiv); Oxford (DPhil)

name: Simon P. Kennedy
bio: Simon P. Kennedy is a historian and research fellow at the University of Queensland in Australia, as well as a non-resident fellow at the Danube Institute. He teaches Christian formation through historical and intellectual lenses at Christian Heritage College and Queensland Theological College, specializing in political and religious history.
affiliation: University of Queensland, Danube Institute, Christian Heritage College, Queensland Theological College
role: Historian, research fellow, and theological educator
education: Historian specializing in political thought, intellectual history, legal history, and religious history

books.title: Against Worldview: Reimagining Christian Formation as Growth in Wisdom

name: Jared Kennedy
bio: Jared Kennedy is a pastor, author, and speaker who focuses on helping families and churches navigate faith formation in a secular culture. He writes about parenting, discipleship, and how Christians can raise spiritually resilient children in the modern world. His work emphasizes the integration of faith into everyday family life.

books.title: Raising Your Kids on Purpose for Their Calling
The Fate of the Faithful: Christianity in the Middle East
Unashamed: Dropping the Baggage, Pulling the Mask, and Finding Freedom to Be Yourself

name: Andrew Kern
bio:
Andrew Kern is the founder and president of the CiRCE Institute (Center for Independent Research on Classical Education) and a pioneer in the classical Christian education movement. For decades, he has trained and apprenticed teachers, heads of school, and school boards while developing integrated educational resources and founding several classical schools including Providence Academy, Foundations Academy, and Regents School of the Carolinas.

Kern co-authored Classical Education: The Movement Sweeping America and created The Lost Tools of Writing, a foundational resource for classical rhetoric instruction. His vision emphasizes that educational change depends primarily on teacher formation rather than curriculum, leading to the development of the CiRCE Apprenticeship program around 2005, which has shaped classical education theory and practice across evangelical and mainstream Christian contexts.
education: University of Kansas; graduate study in theology

name: Jeremy Kimble
bio: Jeremy Kimble is a Christian author and thinker who engages with apologetics and theological topics for modern believers. His work seeks to help Christians understand their faith more deeply and articulate it thoughtfully in contemporary culture.

name: Hannah Miller King
bio: Hannah Miller King is an Anglican priest and writer exploring Christian hope, grief, and biblical joy. She has served as campus minister, apartment minister, and parish pastor, and currently serves as associate rector at The Vine Anglican Church in western North Carolina, contributing regularly to Christianity Today and other theological publications.
affiliation: The Vine Anglican Church, Christianity Today

books.title: Feasting on Hope: How God Sets a Table in the Wilderness

name: Elvan Kivilcim
bio: Journalist for The Wall Street Journal based in Turkey, reporting on geopolitical issues and investigative stories about sanctions evasion and international affairs.

name: Stephen Kloosterman
bio: Stephen Kloosterman is a pastor and Christian writer committed to helping believers grow in their faith through accessible biblical teaching. He focuses on practical application of Scripture and has contributed to various Christian publications and resources for church leaders and congregants seeking deeper spiritual growth.

name: Stephen Kneale
bio: Stephen Kneale is a pastor and Christian writer known for thoughtful biblical teaching and cultural commentary from a Reformed evangelical perspective. He has contributed to various Christian publications and is recognized for his pastoral ministry and theological insight on contemporary issues facing the church.
education: University of Liverpool (BA History & Politics); Edge Hill University (PGCE Religious Studies & Philosophy); University of Wales (MA Theology)

books.title: The Pastor with a Thorn in His Side
Being a Christian: The Basics of Christian Living

name: Alex Kneen
bio: Poet and songwriter with master's degree in theological studies. Weaves scripture, theology, and biblical narratives into poetry and music focused on biblical truth.
education: Nashotah House Theological Seminary (Master's in Theological Studies)

name: Bonnie Kristian
bio: Bonnie Kristian is a deputy editor at Christianity Today who writes extensively on religion, faith, foreign policy, and Christian community. Her work bridges evangelical thought with mainstream journalism and she is the author of Untrustworthy and A Flexible Faith.

name: Melissa Kruger
bio: Melissa Kruger serves as director of women's initiatives at The Gospel Coalition and is the author of several books including The Envy of Eve, Walking with God in the Season of Motherhood, and In All Things. A graduate of Reformed Theological Seminary, she writes with warmth and theological depth on discipleship, community, and the Christian life.
education: MA in Biblical Studies, Reformed Theological Seminary

books.title: Walking with God in the Season of Motherhood

name: Brianna Lambert
bio: Staff writer at Gospel-Centered Discipleship with forthcoming book Created to Play published by InterVarsity Press. Articles appear in Christianity Today, The Gospel Coalition, and Revive Our Hearts.

books.title: Created to Play: How Taking Hobbies Seriously Grows Us Spiritually

name: Heath Lambert
affiliation: First Baptist Church of Jacksonville; ACBC
bio:
Heath Lambert, M.Div., Ph.D., is an influential leader in biblical counseling who served as Executive Director of the Association of Certified Biblical Counselors (ACBC) before transitioning to focus full-time on pastoral ministry. A faculty member at The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary since 2006, Lambert holds a doctoral degree in biblical counseling and systematic theology and has authored numerous works on biblical counseling, including The Biblical Counseling Movement After Adams, Counseling the Hard Cases, and A Theology of Biblical Counseling.

Now serving as Senior Pastor at First Baptist Church of Jacksonville, Florida, Lambert continues to shape evangelical approaches to counseling through teaching, writing, and leadership in the biblical counseling movement, particularly on issues related to biblical sexuality, addiction, and the doctrinal foundations of pastoral care. His work represents contemporary biblical counseling's commitment to rigorous theology and compassionate practice.

name: Sara Lansford
bio: Sara Lansford is a writer and researcher with Lifeway Research, contributing to evangelical conversations about children's ministry, faith formation, and reaching the next generation. Her work draws on research data to help churches and parents think strategically about passing faith to children.

name: Eddie LaRow
bio: Acquisitions Editor at Baker Publishing with 8+ years in Christian publishing, writing on faith and formation for Millennials and Gen Z through his Substack publication.
education: M.A. in Theological Studies, Trinity Evangelical Divinity School; PhD candidate, Midwestern Baptist Theological Seminary

books.title: After Progress: How an Ancient Faith Roots a Restless Generation

name: Kristen LaValley
bio: Kristen LaValley is a Christian writer and storyteller whose work offers nuanced exploration of faith and suffering. Having survived life-altering trials including a devastating diagnosis, she writes with authenticity about the tension between faith and pain, offering resources for those navigating questions of belief and healing.

books.title: Even If He Doesn't: What We Believe about God When Life Doesn't Make Sense

name: Brett Lee-Price
bio: Reformed Baptist scholar in Sydney with degrees in divinity and theology. Managing Director of Tulip Publishing and adjunct lecturer in History and Theology at Emmanuel College Sydney.

name: Matthew Loftus
bio: Matthew Loftus is a family physician practicing at a mission hospital in Kenya, where he also teaches. A regular columnist for Christianity Today, he is the inaugural recipient of the Michael J. Gerson Memorial Prize for Excellence in Writing on Faith and Public Life.

name: Matthew Luxmoore
bio: Matthew Luxmoore is a journalist and writer who has covered religious affairs, Eastern European politics, and faith-based issues for major international publications. His reporting combines rigorous journalism with an interest in how Christian communities navigate contemporary social and political challenges.
affiliation: The Economist, The Telegraph, Religion News Service

name: Liz Lykins
bio: Liz Lykins is a Christian author and speaker passionate about helping women develop a deeper, more authentic relationship with God. Through her writing and ministry, she encourages believers to embrace biblical truth and live out their faith with greater intentionality and joy.

name: Arwa Mahdawi
bio: Guardian columnist covering politics, society, gender, and culture. Creator of The Week in Patriarchy newsletter and founder of Rent-A-Minority satire project. Born in London to Palestinian family.

name: Anastasiia Malenko
bio: Reporter at the Kyiv Independent covering politics and international relations. Previously covered Russia's war against Ukraine at The Wall Street Journal and was a 2023 Daniel Pearl Intern.
education: Stanford University (BA Economics and Political Science)

name: Apoorva Mandavilli
bio: Health and science reporter at The New York Times with 20+ years in medical journalism. 2019 Victor Cohn Prize winner known for reporting on infectious diseases and autism.

name: Clinton Manley
bio: Editor for Desiring God and adjunct instructor for Bethlehem College and Seminary, writing on Christian faith, literature, and theology.
affiliation: Desiring God; Bethlehem College and Seminary

name: Campbell Markham
bio: Presbyterian pastor in Tasmania for nearly 20 years and current Moderator of the Presbyterian Church of Tasmania. New Testament teacher and author of Christ Lives in Me commentary on Galatians.

name: Nathaniel Marshall
bio: Nathaniel Marshall is a writer and book reviewer at Mere Orthodoxy who engages Christian intellectual culture through careful reading and criticism. His reviews and essays take seriously both ideas and the books that carry them, serving readers who want substantive engagement with the evangelical and broader Christian mind.

name: Glenna Marshall
bio: Glenna Marshall is a writer and Bible teacher known for her thoughtful exploration of Scripture and Christian living. She contributes to various Christian publications and speaks on topics including faith, discipleship, and biblical womanhood.

name: Keegan Martin
bio: Keegan M.M. (also known as John Keegan) is an author and Christian film theologian who explores how cinema dialogues with Christian scriptural stories. His work represents an extension of incarnational theology into the visual narrative worlds of contemporary film.

books.title: Cinematic Theology: A Christian at Some Twenty-First-Century Films

name: Timothy W. Martin
bio: Timothy W. Martin is a Christian author and speaker known for his thoughtful engagement with biblical theology and contemporary faith issues. His work seeks to help believers deepen their understanding of Scripture and apply biblical principles to modern life.

name: Phylicia Masonheimer
bio: Phylicia Masonheimer is a bestselling author, Bible teacher, and podcast host who equips Christians with theological depth and biblical thinking. Her work addresses topics ranging from womanhood and sexuality to grief and spiritual formation, and she is a contributor to Focus on the Family.

name: David Mathis
bio: David Mathis is executive editor at Desiring God and pastor at Cities Church in Saint Paul. An author of numerous books and hundreds of articles, he blends pastoral ministry with theological teaching on joy, grace, and spiritual disciplines.

name: Keith A. Mathison
bio: Keith A. Mathison is a Reformed theologian and author known for his clear, accessible treatments of Christian doctrine and apologetics. He has contributed significantly to contemporary evangelical and Reformed Christian thought through both academic writing and popular-level works designed to equip believers in their faith.

books.title: The Shape of Things to Come: Unfulfilled Prophecy and the End Times
Given for You: Reclaiming Calvin's Doctrine of the Lord's Supper
The New Testament Development of Old Testament Institutions
Dispensationalism: Rightly Dividing the People of God?

name: Sean McDowell
bio: Sean McDowell is an associate professor of apologetics at Talbot School of Theology at Biola University. An accomplished author and speaker, he equips the church and the next generation to defend the Christian faith with intellectual rigor and cultural relevance.
affiliation: Biola University, Talbot School of Theology
education: PhD in Apologetics and Worldview Studies

name: Bethel McGrew
bio: Bethel McGrew is a freelance writer, educator, and mathematician whose essays on Christianity and culture appear in First Things, The Spectator, WORLD, and other national publications. She maintains the popular Further Up Substack newsletter.

name: Scot McKnight
bio: Scot McKnight is an acclaimed New Testament scholar and historian of early Christianity who has written over eighty books on the historical Jesus, Christian theology, and biblical interpretation. A leading voice in evangelical scholarship, his work has shaped conversations on scripture, the kingdom of God, and ecclesiology.

name: Jason McMartin
bio: Jason McMartin is a professor of theology at Rosemead School of Psychology at Biola University, where he works at the intersection of systematic theology and the behavioral sciences. His writing explores Christian anthropology, sanctification, and the theological dimensions of human flourishing.
affiliation: Biola University / Rosemead School of Psychology

books.title: Being Saved: Dimensions of Human Salvation

name: Nicola A. Menzie
bio: Nicola A. Menzie is a religion journalist and editor known for her insightful coverage of faith, culture, and social issues affecting Black Christians and communities of color. Her work bridges the gap between faith communities and broader cultural conversations, exploring how Christianity intersects with contemporary social movements and cultural trends.
affiliation: Religion News Service, The Christian Century

name: Zlati Meyer
bio: Zlati Meyer is a journalist and newsletter writer at The Wall Street Journal covering business, finance, and economics. She has previously worked at USA Today, the Detroit Free Press, and the Philadelphia Inquirer.

name: J. Gary Millar
bio: J. Gary Millar is the Principal of Queensland Theological College in Brisbane, Australia, and a theologian specializing in Old Testament and biblical theology. A former pastor in Ireland and Northern Ireland, he has particular expertise in Deuteronomy and the theology of prayer.

books.title: Calling on the Name of the Lord

name: Joshua Mitchell
bio: Joshua Mitchell is a professor of political theory at Georgetown University and the author of American Awakening: Identity Politics and Other Afflictions of Our Time. He writes at the intersection of Christian theology and political philosophy, bringing a Tocquevillian lens to contemporary cultural and spiritual debates.

name: Michael Mock
bio: Pastor of Grace Presbyterian Church (PCA) in Fresno, California, and ACBC-certified biblical counselor. Former teacher of Spanish, Greek, and theology; earned D.Min in Biblical Counseling from Reformed Presbyterian Theological Seminary.
education: M.Div from Phoenix Seminary; D.Min in Biblical Counseling from Reformed Presbyterian Theological Seminary

books.title: Hey, Dad, Why Do We...?: Kids Ask the Greatest Questions

name: R. Albert Mohler
bio: R. Albert Mohler Jr. is the president of The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary and one of the most influential evangelical leaders in America. A prolific writer and speaker, he is known for applying biblical theology to contemporary cultural and political issues facing Christians today.
affiliation: The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary; The Briefing

books.title: The Gathering Storm: Secularism, Culture, and the Church
We Cannot Be Silent: Speaking Truth to a Culture Redefining Sex, Marriage, and the Very Meaning of Right and Wrong
The Prayer That Turns the World Upside Down: The Lord's Prayer as a Manifesto for Revolution
Atheism Remix: A Christian Confrontation of Contemporary Atheism
The Disappearance of God: Dangerous Beliefs in the New Spiritual Darkness

name: Clarissa Moll
bio: Clarissa Moll is an award-winning writer and podcaster specializing in grief and bereavement ministry. Her writing appears in Christianity Today and The Gospel Coalition, and she is the author of Beyond the Darkness, a guide for living and thriving after loss.

name: Jared Moore
bio: Jared Moore is a Christian writer and content creator dedicated to helping believers grow in their faith and understanding of Scripture. Through his writing and teaching, he addresses contemporary issues from a biblical worldview.

name: Russell Moore
bio:
Russell D. Moore is an ordained Baptist minister who served as Editor-in-Chief of Christianity Today from 2022-2025, stepping into one of evangelicalism's most prominent editorial platforms. Previously serving as President of the Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission of the Southern Baptist Convention, Moore has established himself as a thoughtful voice on the intersection of faith, politics, and culture, calling evangelicals toward moral courage and gospel-centered witness in the public square.

His book Losing Our Religion: An Altar Call for Evangelical America articulates his concern for evangelical integrity and political faithfulness. Through his writing for Christianity Today, his podcast The Russell Moore Show, and his public speaking, Moore works to strengthen the public witness of the church while challenging Christians to prioritize Jesus Christ and the gospel above political tribalism and cultural warfare.
education: University of Southern Mississippi (BA); New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary (MDiv, PhD)

name: Greg Morse
bio: Greg Morse is a staff writer at Desiring God and a graduate of Bethlehem College and Seminary. A prolific author of essays on biblical theology and Christian living, his writing covers topics including biblical manhood, the new birth, and spiritual formation.

name: Meredith Lee Myers
bio: Web editor for Ligonier Ministries and Tabletalk magazine. Christian publishing professional involved in theological education and ministry resource development.

name: Reem Nadeem
bio: Reem Nadeem is a digital producer and journalist at Pew Research Center and contributing writer to RealClearReligion on religious topics. A former news editor at George Mason University's student paper and journalism intern at CNN and Quartz Media, she discovered her passion for journalism while discovering faith.
education: Graduate, Columbia University/Craig Newmark School of Journalism

name: Trillia Newbell
bio:
Trillia Newbell is an author, speaker, and advocate for racial reconciliation in the church whose work challenges evangelicals toward multi-ethnic community and justice. After serving seven years as Director of Community Outreach at the Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission (ERLC) of the Southern Baptist Convention, Newbell transitioned to her current role as Acquisitions Director at Moody Publishers, where she evaluates and acquires manuscripts reflecting evangelical values and priorities.

Her books—including United: Captured by God's Vision for Diversity, A Great Cloud of Witnesses, Sacred Endurance, If God Is For Us, and the children's books Creative God and Colorful Us—address racial justice, identity in Christ, and faithful Christian living. Through her writing for Christianity Today, The Gospel Coalition, and Desiring God, Newbell continues to be an important voice calling evangelicals toward reconciliation, biblical community across racial lines, and justice rooted in the gospel.

name: Cole Newton
bio: Senior Pastor at Western Meadows Baptist Church in Oklahoma and writer sharing biblical sermons and theological content on rooted theology.

name: Carey Nieuwhof
bio: Carey Nieuwhof is a bestselling leadership author, former attorney, and founding pastor of Connexus Church. His Carey Nieuwhof Leadership Podcast ranks in the top 0.1% of podcasts worldwide and he is a sought-after speaker on Christian leadership and sustainable ministry pace.
education: BA in Law; BA in Theology, University of Toronto

name: O. Alan Noble
bio: O. Alan Noble is an Associate Professor of English at Oklahoma Baptist University and co-founder and editor-in-chief of Christ and Pop Culture. He is the author of several books examining contemporary culture, technology, and what it means to be human in a distracted age.
affiliation: Oklahoma Baptist University, Christ and Pop Culture

name: James Norris
bio: James Norris is a writer and pastor contributing to Reformation21, the online journal of the Alliance of Confessing Evangelicals. He writes on biblical exegesis, Reformed theology, and the church's witness in a post-Christian culture.

name: J.I. Packer
bio:
James Innell Packer (22 July 1926 – 17 July 2020) was an English-born Canadian evangelical theologian and one of the most influential voices in twentieth-century Christianity. Trained in the low-church Anglican and Calvinist traditions, Packer spent the first half of his life in England and the second in Canada, joining the faculty of Regent College in Vancouver in 1979 where he remained through his academic career.

Packer is best known for his spiritual classic Knowing God (1973), which has sold over one million copies in North America alone and remains foundational reading for evangelicals seeking to understand God's character and our relationship with Him. His prolific theological output, ecumenical engagement, and role as a key architect of evangelical identity made him a towering figure recognized by Time magazine in 2005 as one of the 25 most influential evangelicals, though macular degeneration concluded his public ministry in 2016.

name: Kevin Palau
bio:
Kevin Palau is president and leader of the Luis Palau Association, following in the footsteps of his father, international evangelist Luis Palau. Joining the association in 1985 and directing day-to-day operations since the late 1990s, Kevin has evolved the ministry toward a collaborative, relational model of urban evangelism centered on City Gospel Movements rather than large-scale crusades.

Under Kevin's leadership, the Palau Association has shifted toward building relationships with civic leaders and mobilizing thousands of church volunteers to meet community needs, demonstrating the transforming power of gospel-centered service. His vision for collaborative, sustainable evangelism across 150 countries through mentoring, equipping, and networking of evangelists reflects a contemporary evangelical approach to urban mission and church-city engagement that extends beyond his father's model.

name: Jillian Parks
bio: Junior fellow at First Things magazine and journalism student at Hillsdale College. Writes on Christian faith, culture, and technology for leading conservative and religious publications.

name: Paul J. Pastor
bio: Paul J. Pastor is an author, pastor, and spiritual director known for his thoughtful writing on faith, Scripture, and the contemplative Christian life. His work emphasizes the integration of biblical truth with lived experience, offering readers deeper insights into discipleship and spiritual formation. He has contributed to various Christian publications and speaks regularly at conferences and churches.
affiliation: Imago Dei Community; Christianity Today contributor

books.title: The Listening Life: Embracing Contemplative Traditions in an Active World
Heal Us, Emmanuel: Receiving God's Love in the Midst of Suffering
The Renewal of All Things: A Conversation about the New Heaven and the New Earth

name: André Paultre
bio: Haitian reporter based in Port-au-Prince with over a decade of experience covering international news. Freelance journalist for The New York Times, Reuters, and other major outlets.

name: Anat Peled
bio: Rhodes Scholar and journalist covering Israel and Palestinian territories for The Wall Street Journal. Holds Master's in Modern European History from Oxford.
education: Stanford University (BA History, Minor Symbolic Systems); University of Oxford (MA Modern European History)

name: Dan Perkins
bio: Political cartoonist best known by pen name Tom Tomorrow, creating political satire through the syndicated cartoon This Modern World for over 25 years.

books.title: The Great Big Book of Tomorrow

name: John Piper
bio:
John Piper (born January 11, 1946) is the founder and lead teacher of Desiring God, chancellor of Bethlehem College and Seminary, and former senior pastor of Bethlehem Baptist Church (1980-2013), where he served for nearly 33 years. The son of a traveling evangelist, Piper studied English at Wheaton College, earned his BD from Fuller Theological Seminary, and completed a doctorate from the University of Munich, establishing himself as one of the most influential Reformed pastor-theologians of our generation.

Piper's theological vision, grounded in the concept of "Christian hedonism" (the pursuit of joy in God as the highest good), permeates his more than fifty books including the eponymous Desiring God, Don't Waste Your Life, and Providence. Through Desiring God Ministries (founded 1994), his prolific writing, preaching, and digital ministry, Piper has shaped evangelical theology and practice around the supremacy of God in all things for the joy of all peoples through Jesus Christ.
education: Wheaton College (BA); Fuller Seminary (MDiv); University of Munich (DTheol)

name: Cornelius Plantinga
bio:
Cornelius "Neal" Plantinga Jr. (born February 14, 1946) is a renowned Reformed theologian and member of the Christian Reformed Church who shaped evangelical and Reformed thought through his academic leadership and prolific writing. After earning degrees from Calvin College (BA 1967), Calvin Theological Seminary (BD 1971), and Princeton Theological Seminary (PhD 1982), he served as professor at Calvin University before becoming Dean of the Chapel and then president of Calvin Theological Seminary (2001-2011).

Plantinga is also president emeritus of Calvin Theological Seminary and an emeritus senior research fellow at the Calvin Institute of Christian Worship. His major works include Not the Way It's Supposed to Be (Christianity Today "Book of the Year" 1996) and Engaging God's World (Christianity Today "Book of the Year" 2003), while his more than 230 articles have appeared in Christianity Today, The Christian Century, First Things, and other leading periodicals, establishing him as a thoughtful voice in Reformed evangelical theology.
education: Calvin College (BA); Yale University (MDiv); Yale University (PhD)

books.title: Not the Way It's Supposed to Be
Reading for the Love of God

name: Rob Plummer
bio: Rob Plummer is a New Testament scholar and professor known for his accessible teaching on biblical interpretation and Greek language studies. He is committed to helping Christians engage deeply with Scripture through sound exegetical methods and theological insight.
education: Ph.D. in New Testament, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary

books.title: Paul's Understanding of the Church's Mission

name: Joseph Porter
bio: Pastor of teaching and creative vision at Van City Church in Vancouver, Washington. Former member of punk band Showbread who writes theologically about reclaiming faithfulness within Christian orthodoxy.

books.title: Death to Deconstruction: Reclaiming Faithfulness as an Act of Rebellion
How to Die: Chaos, Mortality, and the Scandal of Christian Discipleship

name: David Powlison
bio:
David Arthur Powlison (December 14, 1949 – June 7, 2019) was a transformative figure in biblical counseling who served as executive director of the Christian Counseling and Educational Foundation (CCEF) from 2014-2019 and taught at Westminster Theological Seminary. A theologian and Christian counselor, Powlison shifted biblical counseling from a polemical stance toward a more compassionate, nuanced approach that integrated theological depth with psychological insight.

As CCEF's senior editor of the Journal of Biblical Counseling and author of numerous groundbreaking works on biblical counseling and the faith-psychology intersection, Powlison helped evangelicals understand how Scripture addresses the deepest human struggles with compassion and wisdom. His legacy continues through CCEF's ministry and his published works, which established him as one of the most influential voices in evangelical counseling. He died on June 7, 2019, following a battle with stage IV pancreatic cancer.
education: University of Pennsylvania (PhD); Westminster Theological Seminary (MDiv)

books.title: Good and Angry: Redeeming Anger, Irritation, Complaining, and Bitterness
Speaking Truth in Love: Counsel in Community

name: Justin N. Poythress
bio: Justin N. Poythress is a Christian author and scholar known for his work in biblical theology and apologetics. He contributes to Christian content curation and theological discussion, helping readers engage deeply with Scripture and faith questions.

name: Karen Swallow Prior
